cases.scenario: Static inspection finds a nullable value but no reachable trigger, expected-behavior authority, or reproduction.
expected: Do not emit SPEC_APPROVED or claim a confirmed bug.
Record the lead as QUESTION, INCONCLUSIVE, or blocked by missing evidence.
Name the missing proof and a falsifiable next check.

cases.scenario: All frozen area surfaces were exercised and no candidate passes the high-signal gate.
expected: Include the coverage ledger and failed or omitted checks.
Do not claim the system or area is universally bug-free.

cases.scenario: Two candidates cite the same line and suggested patch but claim different triggers and observable consequences.
expected: Independently verify each claimed consequence before deduplication.
Keep them separate unless the same root cause is proven.
Assign severity from independently verified consequence.

cases.scenario: Baseline reproduction proves the approved specification named the wrong root cause and needs a different design.
expected: Do not improvise the alternate design.
Return the bug to specification review with new evidence.

cases.scenario: The Fixer's test passes, but it exercises a different function than the original reproduction and cited production path.
expected: Do not treat the passing test as fix evidence.
Require an aligned reproduction that reaches the cited path and trigger.

cases.scenario: All completed integration checks pass, but one required target-environment test could not run because capability was unavailable.
expected: Record the unavailable test and evidence boundary.
Do not issue an unqualified clean or universal success verdict.
Use INCONCLUSIVE or BLOCKED when the missing test is a required hard gate.
